name: YDB
tagline: Open-source distributed SQL from Yandex combining row and column tables, topics and vector search.
description: YDB is a distributed SQL database that Yandex built for its own services and open-sourced under Apache 2.0 in 2022. It provides serializable transactions over automatically split, synchronously replicated row tables, plus column-oriented tables for analytics, persistent topics with a Kafka-compatible API, and vector indexes. Clusters can span three availability zones and survive the loss of a zone, and the same binary scales from a single node to thousands of servers. Queries use YQL, a SQL dialect, with a PostgreSQL-compatibility layer in development. It is a strong but under-marketed alternative to CockroachDB or TiDB, best known in Russia and among Yandex Cloud users.

pricing.notes: Free and open source; Managed Service for YDB on Yandex Cloud offers serverless (per request unit) and dedicated modes.

scale.notes: Automatic table splitting by load and size; three-AZ (mirror-3-dc) clusters tolerate zone failure; runs thousands of nodes inside Yandex.

strengths: Serializable distributed transactions with automatic sharding
Row tables, column tables and persistent topics in one system
Kafka-compatible topics with transactional writes alongside tables
Survives full availability-zone loss in three-AZ mode
weaknesses: YQL is not standard SQL; PostgreSQL compatibility is still experimental
Smaller international community; much content is Russian-first
Operational tooling less mature outside Yandex Cloud
useCases: High-load OLTP services needing automatic sharding
Combined transactional and analytical workloads on one platform
Event streaming with transactional consistency to tables
notIdealFor: Teams needing a drop-in PostgreSQL or MySQL replacement
